root_cause.text: The IPv4 multipath hash sysctl code incorrectly used READ_ONCE()/WRITE_ONCE() on the whole 8-byte `struct sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed`, even though the struct is only 4-byte aligned, causing ARM64 Clang-LTO to generate misaligned 64-bit acquire loads and non-atomic split stores on that struct.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `READ_ONCE(net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed).mp_seed` to `READ_ONCE(net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed.mp_seed)`, and replaces `WRITE_ONCE(net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed, new)` with two 32-bit member `WRITE_ONCE()` calls; the commit message states the struct has “an 8-byte structure with a 4-byte alignment requirement,” that Clang LTO emitted a 64-bit `ldar` causing an ARM64 alignment fault, and that whole-struct `WRITE_ONCE()` was split into two 32-bit stores, “destroy[ing] atomicity and expos[ing] a tear-write vulnerability.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Read the fib multipath hash seed field with READ_ONCE directly to ensure the seed value is accessed correctly and safely.
intent_record.what: The code changes the READ_ONCE argument from `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed` followed by `.mp_seed` outside the macro to `net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed.mp_seed`, moving the `mp_seed` field access inside the READ_ONCE call.
intent_record.how: This makes the read operate atomically on the `mp_seed` field itself rather than on the containing object expression, ensuring the hash seed value is fetched as a single READ_ONCE-protected access and avoiding incorrect or unsafe access semantics.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the multipath hash seed by writing its scalar fields individually with WRITE_ONCE instead of assigning the whole structure at once.
intent_record.what: The single WRITE_ONCE assignment that wrote the entire net->ipv4.sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed object from new was replaced with two WRITE_ONCE calls that separately assign the user_seed and mp_seed fields from new.user_seed and new.mp_seed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now updates each member of the multipath hash seed structure individually instead of performing one whole-structure write, ensuring the seed values are stored through WRITE_ONCE in a way appropriate for scalar fields and avoiding incorrect or unsupported atomic-style assignment of the full struct.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use READ_ONCE when fetching the multipath hash user seed to guard against concurrent unsynchronized reads.
intent_record.what: The code changes the assignment of `user_seed` from a direct read of `mphs->user_seed` to a `READ_ONCE(mphs->user_seed)` access in `proc_fib_multipath_hash_seed()`.
intent_record.how: This makes the read of `mphs->user_seed` use single-copy access semantics, reducing the chance of races or inconsistent reads when the value may be modified concurrently, while preserving the surrounding logic and data flow.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make fib multipath hash seed access concurrency-safe by using READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE on its scalar fields instead of unsafely reading or assigning the structure directly.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by avoiding READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE on the misaligned 8-byte struct and instead using per-field scalar READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE accesses, preventing the problematic misaligned 64-bit loads/stores.

The change directly modifies how the multipath hash user seed is read using READ_ONCE(), which is the exact mechanism involved in the root cause: incorrect READ_ONCE()/WRITE_ONCE() use on the misaligned 8-byte sysctl seed struct.

candidates.rationale: This writes the entire 8-byte struct with WRITE_ONCE even though the struct is only 4-byte aligned, directly matching the root cause of misaligned 64-bit stores and non-atomic split stores.
This performs READ_ONCE on the whole struct expression before selecting mp_seed, causing an unsafe misaligned 64-bit load from the 4-byte aligned struct, which is the read side of the root cause.

This unsynchronized field read is part of the same concurrency-sensitive access path to the struct and was later guarded with READ_ONCE, though it is less direct than the whole-struct READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE misuse.

vuln_statements.explanation: This applies READ_ONCE to the entire 8-byte sysctl_fib_multipath_hash_seed struct before accessing mp_seed. Because that struct is only 4-byte aligned, this can compile into a misaligned 64-bit load, matching the root cause.

This applies WRITE_ONCE to the whole 8-byte struct, even though the struct is only 4-byte aligned. That can produce misaligned 64-bit stores or non-atomic split stores, which is the write-side of the root cause.
